privacy.section2Intro: When you use Learnstation, we process the following personal data:
section2Items: <bold>Account data:</bold> email address, password (stored encrypted), name (optional), university and programme (optional), avatar picture (optional), preferred language.
<bold>Learning progress:</bold> completed pages, quiz results, XP, level, streaks and achievements.
<bold>Learning events:</bold> reading time per page, quiz answers with timestamps and self-rated understanding.
<bold>What you write:</bold> questions to the AI tutor and the conversation history, your written explanations in practice, search queries, notes and feedback messages.
<bold>Documents you upload:</bold> the files, the text extracted from them and the summaries and questions generated from that text.
<bold>Social data:</bold> friend connections and friend requests, and whether you appear on the leaderboard.
<bold>Technical data:</bold> IP address, browser type and the pages you request, in server logs and error reports kept for a short time.
section3Items: <bold>Performance of contract (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR):</bold> account data, learning progress, your uploads and the AI features (summaries, questions, tutor answers) are required to provide the service you signed up for.

<bold>Legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR):</bold> learning events are collected to improve teaching and to show the people who maintain a Space where learners struggle; server logs and error reports are kept to run the service securely and reliably.
section4Items: <bold>Supabase Inc.</bold> — sign-in, database and file storage.
<bold>Hetzner Online GmbH (Germany)</bold> — hosting of the application server.

<bold>AI providers</bold> — to generate summaries, questions and tutor answers, the text of your documents, your questions and your conversation history are sent to <bold>OpenAI</bold>. Depending on the server configuration, <bold>Groq</bold>, <bold>Google (Gemini)</bold>, <bold>Cloudflare</bold>, <bold>Mistral</bold> and <bold>OpenRouter</bold> can be used as fallbacks for the same purpose. Your name and email address are not part of these requests.
<bold>LlamaIndex (LlamaParse)</bold> — when that parsing engine is selected, uploaded documents are sent there to extract their text.
<bold>Microsoft (Edge text-to-speech)</bold> — text is sent to produce spoken audio when you use the read-aloud feature.

<bold>Sentry (Functional Software, Inc.)</bold> — error monitoring. Error reports contain technical data about the failure (browser, page, device); identifying fields are removed before sending. There is no session recording.
<bold>Resend, Inc.</bold> — transactional email, for example when you send feedback.
privacy.section5Body: Your data is stored as long as your account is active. After account deletion, all personal data is deleted within 30 days. AI tutor conversations and learning events are kept for as long as your account exists. Server logs and error reports are kept for a short period only.
privacy.section6Intro: Under the GDPR, you have the following rights:
section6Items: <bold>Right of access (Art. 15):</bold> you can request what data we have stored about you.
<bold>Right to erasure (Art. 17):</bold> you can delete your account and all associated data in the settings.
<bold>Right to data portability (Art. 20):</bold> you can export your data as a JSON file in the settings.
<bold>Right to object (Art. 21):</bold> you may object to the processing of your data at any time.
<bold>Right to lodge a complaint:</bold> you have the right to file a complaint with a data protection authority.
privacy.section7Body: Learnstation does not use <bold>tracking cookies</bold> or advertising trackers (no Google Analytics, no Facebook Pixel). Only the browser's localStorage is used for session management and settings. Error monitoring (see processors) receives technical error data without a session recording.
privacy.section8Body: Some processors listed above are based in the United States or may process data there (Supabase, OpenAI, Groq, Google, Cloudflare, Mistral, OpenRouter, LlamaIndex, Microsoft, Sentry, Resend). For these transfers the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) or the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework apply as safeguards under Art. 46 GDPR.
